articles.excerpt: If you build or run a website, you probably test it from where you sit. For cookie banners and trackers, that means you see one version of your site, and visitors in other countries may see a very dif…
articles.body: If you build or run a website, you probably test it from where you sit. For cookie banners and trackers, that means you see one version of your site, and visitors in other countries may see a very different one. We wanted to know how different, so we measured it. (General information, not legal advice.) What we did On 14 October 2026 we loaded the same websites, on the same day, with the same scanner settings, from two places: a server in Virginia (US) and a server in Frankfurt (Germany, EU) . The sites: a seeded random sample of popular websites from Google's Chrome UX Report list. 200 of them loaded from both places, so all numbers below compare those 200. Homepage only, one visit each, as a first-time visitor: no cookies, and nobody clicked the cookie banner .

articles.title: How do you red team MCP agents?
articles.excerpt: Red teaming MCP agents: the core idea Red teaming MCP agents comes down to one idea: attack your own agent through its tools before someone else does. Most MCP security testing checks OAuth, tokens an…
articles.body: Red teaming MCP agents: the core idea Red teaming MCP agents comes down to one idea: attack your own agent through its tools before someone else does. Most MCP security testing checks OAuth, tokens and transport. That work matters, but it does not show whether your agent will follow a hidden instruction planted in a tool description, a changed tool or a tool's output. Server layer vs model layer MCP security has two layers, and most testing covers only one. Server layer. Checks whether the server and its connections are built correctly: confused deputy, token passthrough, session hijacking, SSRF, local server security and scope minimization. These are identity and infrastructure checks. Model layer. Checks what the agent does once it reads a tool's description or output.

articles.title: Compare salaries and hiring across countries with Glassdoor job data and Python
articles.excerpt: "What does a data analyst earn in London compared to New York?" sounds like a question with an easy answer. In practice salary data is scattered across reports with different dates, definitions and sa…
articles.body: "What does a data analyst earn in London compared to New York?" sounds like a question with an easy answer. In practice salary data is scattered across reports with different dates, definitions and samples. Live job postings are a decent alternative: they show what employers are advertising right now, and Glassdoor shows a salary range for most of its listings. In this tutorial we'll write one Python script (~70 lines) that: runs the same Glassdoor search in four cities in four countries, in parallel, saves every posting to a CSV, uses pandas to compare yearly pay ranges, how many postings list a salary at all, and which companies are hiring. The example is "data analyst" in New York, London, Berlin and Bengaluru. Swap in any role and any locations Glassdoor covers.

articles.title: GMO investigates Onamae data leak as Artex connection remains unproven
articles.excerpt: Don't Blame the AI for GMO's Breach — Yet Verdict: a real breach at a Japanese cloud provider is being dressed up as an "AI attack" before anyone has proved the AI part. The hype is outrunning the evi…
articles.body: Don't Blame the AI for GMO's Breach — Yet Verdict: a real breach at a Japanese cloud provider is being dressed up as an "AI attack" before anyone has proved the AI part. The hype is outrunning the evidence, and that's the story. GMO Internet is investigating a suspected breach of its Onamae cloud desktop service — 27,000 servers potentially affected, customers reporting unauthorized activity on trading accounts, and an extortion demand of about 8 billion yen on the table. That's serious on its own. It doesn't need an AI villain stapled to it. But the AI angle is exactly where the reporting gets sloppy, and sloppy attribution is how the industry keeps learning the wrong lessons. The facts are bad enough without the AI garnish Trading desktops are a worst-case target.

articles.title: How 'spacewalking' underwater made me feel like I was really in space
articles.excerpt: Analog Astronaut Commander and Aquanaut Michaela Musilova led underwater simulated “spacewalks” in low visibility to test astronaut safety and communication protocols during simulated space missions.
articles.body: I was breathing just fine through my life support systems, but I kept feeling an urge to double check that everything was ok with my "spacesuit" before heading out on this "spacewalk." I have worn many different types of spacesuits on Earth during my career, but for the first time in my life, I knew that I couldn’t just stop to breathe the air outside if there were an emergency. That's because I was underwater. On this excursion, I was leading a simulated space mission underwater called SEA STAR. My " spacesuit " was actually scuba diving gear, and the simulated spacewalks , or EVAs (Extra-Vehicular Activities), included outings where we explored underwater environments.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.

articles.title: Cowboy Space unveils 'Big Iron' rocket to launch 20,000 AI data centers
articles.excerpt: Cowboy Space just gave us our first look at its "Big Iron" rocket, which the company will use to build its AI data center constellation. Big Iron's debut is targeted for late 2028.
articles.body: PALO ALTO, Calif. — Cowboy Space just showed us how it plans to become a big player in the final frontier. The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). It will build those satellites in house and launch them on a homegrown rocket — a vehicle Cowboy Space unveiled here on Monday night (Oct. 26), at an event it called "Big Sky Rising." "It's a fundamentally novel approach to rocketry in the modern era, in our opinion," Bhatt said during the event. "The idea is that you have a two-stage rocket where the upper stage of the rocket itself transforms into the satellite." Big Iron's first stage will be reusable.

articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.

articles.title: NASA’s Neo Surveyor Sunshade
articles.excerpt: A technician inspects the large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission in this image released on Oct. 26, 2026. The sunshade structure, which stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and me…
articles.body: BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems A technician inspects the large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission in this image released on Oct. 26, 2026. The sunshade structure , which stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and measures 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide at its base, will keep the infrared space telescope cool as it searches for near-Earth asteroids and comets while also providing the spacecraft with power. When in space, NEO Surveyor will detect some of the hardest-to-find asteroids and comets, some of which may be located in the direction of the Sun — a region of sky where ground-based optical telescopes have a harder time searching.
